title: 15 · Computing, memory, power and interface silicon

paras: The internal architecture of digital devices, from executable instructions and volatile/nonvolatile memory to power regulation, physical buses and virtual network interfaces.

Reading key: “From the original page” paraphrases the handwritten source; “Technical expansion and corrections” is editorial explanation, not part of the manuscript. Original scans are reproduced unchanged and embedded for offline use.
Technical correction policy: detailed mechanisms, examples and verification in the corrections handbook

blocks.h2: 01 · Processing and computing chips — the brain
paras: From the original pages: The page lists CPU, GPU, MCU, TPU, NPU, DSP, ASIC and FPGA, with functions: execute instructions, perform calculations, run operating systems/software, control logic and manage execution.

Technical expansion and corrections: CPU is a general-purpose instruction executor; GPU excels at parallel workloads; DSP handles signal-processing pipelines; NPU/TPU accelerate neural-network operations; MCU combines processor, memory and peripherals for embedded control. ASIC is a custom fixed-function implementation; FPGA uses reconfigurable logic. These categories overlap: a SoC can contain several of them.

System walkthrough: A web request enters through NIC → kernel network stack → application code running on CPU; cryptography may use CPU instructions or accelerators; a GPU/NPU is used only when the workload calls for it.

blocks.h2: 02 · Memory and storage chips — where values and instructions live
paras: From the original pages: The notes separate working/volatile memory from persistent/nonvolatile memory, listing SRAM, DRAM, FRAM, EDO, SDRAM, DDR/DDR2, GDDR, HBM and ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, flash/NOR/NAND.

Technical expansion and corrections: SRAM commonly implements caches; DRAM implements main memory; GDDR/HBM are bandwidth-oriented memory families. EDO is a legacy DRAM generation, SDRAM denotes synchronous DRAM and DDR is a family of SDRAM. FRAM is nonvolatile, so it must not be placed unqualified in the volatile category. NOR and NAND flash retain data without power; SSDs combine NAND flash with a controller. ROM/PROM/EPROM/EEPROM differ in programmability and erasure. Volatile memory usually loses its working state without power, but power loss does not guarantee secure erasure of every remnant.
System walkthrough: Code on SSD → loaded into RAM → CPU caches → CPU registers and execution → modified data written back to storage when explicitly persisted.

From the original pages: The page describes PMIC, DC-DC, LDO, VRM and battery-charging ICs as electrical gatekeepers that take input from wall power or batteries and distribute stable rails to silicon. It distinguishes static/base power from dynamic demand.

Technical expansion and corrections: A PMIC coordinates power sequencing, charging, monitoring and rails; a VRM is a regulator module supplying processor rails; a DC-DC converter changes DC voltage; an LDO regulates with a linear dropout stage. Power demand varies with voltage, clock frequency, activity and leakage. “Static” and “dynamic” are power-consumption components, not two exclusive kinds of regulator.
System walkthrough: Battery/adapter → PMIC and converters → regulated voltage rails → CPU, RAM, radio, SSD. Voltage stability and thermal constraints influence clock throttling and reliability.

From the original pages: The notes group guided internal PCB traces (PCIe and SATA/NVMe), guided external plugs/cables (display, Ethernet, USB, CAN), and unguided external links (modem, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth). They mention SmartNIC, DPU and NIC.

Technical expansion and corrections: PCIe is a high-speed interconnect; NVMe is a storage command protocol commonly transported over PCIe, while SATA is a separate storage interface. Ethernet MAC and PHY are distinct functions: MAC frames and addresses traffic, PHY handles physical signaling. USB controllers manage protocol transactions, and USB-C is a connector that can support multiple modes. CAN is a bus protocol. Wireless radios use RF front ends, baseband processing and antennas. SmartNICs/DPUs can offload networking and security tasks, but are not required for every NIC.

System walkthrough: Application data → OS network stack → NIC MAC/PHY → cable or RF medium → peer NIC → peer OS/application. Physical bits, frames, packets and application messages belong to different layers.

blocks.h2: 06 · Connected mental model: how a complete system works
paras: Power input → PMIC / DC-DC / VRM → regulated rails ↓ Persistent NAND / SSD → RAM → CPU caches → CPU / GPU / accelerator ↓ PCIe / USB / Ethernet controller ↓ MAC → PHY → copper / fiber / RF ↓ Linux host ↔ bridge ↔ veth ↔ container Every arrow represents a different dependency, not necessarily a direct physical wire: storage supplies persistent bytes; RAM holds active data; processors execute instructions; controllers adapt device-specific transactions; and NICs convert between digital frames and physical signaling. Kernel drivers and protocols coordinate the path.
